ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (Panama AML/CFT framework; creates the Unidad de Análisis Financiero, UAF); Executive Decree 526 of 23 April 2015 (implementing regulations); Law 129 of 11 December 2020 (mandatory customer due diligence, PEP and source-of-funds due diligence); Law 70 of 23 October 2019 and its implementing rules (Beneficial Owner Registry, Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, administered under the Registro Público de Panamá). Corporate-law base: Law 32 of 1927 as amended by Law 4 of 2016.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961, in force for Panama) issued through the Ministerio de Gobierno; consular legalization only if the receiving authority is in a non-Hague state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Existence and Good Standing (Certificado de Personería Jurídica)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Ministerio de Gobierno or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney from each director and shareholder to the resident agent (Poder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the signatory's country of origin or Panamanian notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille; consular legalization where the grantor's state is not party to the Apostille Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, US OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions, and Panamanian competent-authority alerts (UAF and Registro Público). PEP determination is required at onboarding and periodically; domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates are subject to enhanced customer due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Any match on sanctions lists requires immediate blocking, no-dealing instruction, and filing with the UAF in accordance with Law 23/2015 and Law 129/2020.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (RPP) online corporate name-reservation module 'Reserva de Nombre', accessible via https://www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in Panama may be expressed in Spanish or any Latin-script language. Where the intended name originates in a non-Latin script (e.g., Cyrillic, CJK or Arabic script), a compulsory Latin-script transliteration and, where required, a Spanish-language equivalency note must be filed with the reservation, and the transliterated form becomes the operative registered name. The full corporate name must include a corporate designator by full expression or recognized abbreviation (e.g., Sociedad Anónima, S.A., Corporation, Corp., Incorporated, Inc., Limited, Ltd.) as accepted under Law 32/1927.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANCO, BANK, FINANCIERA, CRÉDITO or any financial-intermediation token (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos)
SEGUROS, REASEGUROS, INSURANCE or reinsurance-brokerage equivalents (requires prior licensing clearance from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros)
FIDEICOMISO, TRUST, FIDUCIARIA or fiduciary-services tokens (requires express clearance from the competent Panamanian authority)
CASINO, JUEGOS, GAMING, APUESTAS, LOTERÍA or gaming tokens (requires prior authorization from the Junta de Control de Juegos)
Tokens implying official state affiliation: NACIONAL, MINISTERIO, PRESIDENCIA, GOBIERNO, ESTADO DE PANAMÁ (permitted only with prior written ministerial authorization)
Use of 'PANAMÁ' or sovereign-symbol derivatives that suggest official state sponsorship or patronage
Names identical or deceptively similar to an already-registered Panamanian legal person, trade name, or third-party protected mark
Offensive, misleading, or names contrary to public order and good customs under Registro Público administrative practice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of rejection, the applicant may (i) immediately file an alternative name reservation, and/or (ii) submit a written reconsideration (recurso de reconsideración) to the Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá within five (5) working days of the rejection notice, stating grounds of non-confusion and supplying corrected naming evidence. If the reconsideration is denied, a hierarchical administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) may be filed within five (5) working days of the denial, to be resolved by the Registrar-General or, in appropriate cases, through the administrative chamber of the First Judicial Circuit. The applicant may also seek release of a blocking name by filing a third-party consent letter (constancia) from the conflicting registrant. Reserved names that expire without renewal become available for re-reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited virtual-office arrangement permissible: the company must appoint and continuously maintain a licensed Panamanian resident agent with a physical office inside Panama; correspondence routing and mail-forwarding may be handled through a registered virtual address, but the statutory registered-office address must be a real, serviceable physical location where process, judicial writs and administrative notices can be served. For this low-risk B2B MRO catalog e-commerce entity with no local employees, physical inventory or branch establishment, a virtual back-office supplemented by the resident agent's physical office address is accepted by the Registro Público and the UAF without creating additional fiscal registration obligations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: probability of an unannounced physical or documentary inspection is estimated at approximately 5-7% per annum for a Low_Risk_Standard, non-financial, non-licensed e-commerce company. The likelihood materially increases (estimated 15-25% per annum) if the entity opens a Panamanian bank account, processes frequent or high-value SWIFT wires, or exhibits unusual UBO, PEP or sanctions-related red flags triggering enhanced due diligence by the UAF or institutions regulated by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama Companies Act, Law 32 of 1927, as amended by Law 5 of 2019 (Ley General de Sociedades); Articles 1-10, 15, 16-18, 25, 71-73
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) – Mercantile Section (Sección Registro Mercantil)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública Constitutiva (public deed of incorporation) or private document executed by the founders and presented for registration through the Ventanilla Única de Empresas (VUE)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. One or more shares of no par value may be issued upon subscription; the authorized capital must be fully subscribed, but payment may be deferred. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: At the first board meeting of PA_CORP, S.A., held at the registered office in Panama City on [date], the following resolutions are adopted: (1) The share subscription report is approved and the issuance of one hundred common shares at US$1.00 per share is ratified. (2) The registered office at [address], Panama City, Panamá, and the appointment of registered agent [name] are confirmed. (3) [name] is appointed President, [name] is appointed Secretary, and [name] is appointed Treasurer, jointly authorized to open bank accounts, sign commercial documents, and appoint attorneys. (4) The officers are directed to obtain the municipal operation permit, RUC, fire certificate, and all environmental clearances necessary for the Company's electronic B2B catalog activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section (Ventanilla Electrónica / VUE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic or written application with up to three proposed corporate names in Spanish, specifying the entity type S.A. Pay the reservation fee and obtain the Certificado de No Homónimo (name certificate) valid for 30 days. Prepare the draft by-laws and shareholder information for notarization.
required_dossiers: Application form for corporate name reservation
Proposed corporate name in Spanish
Identification documents of the incorporators or their attorney-in-fact
Notarized power of attorney if using a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected or obstructed by a homonym, the registrant may immediately select an alternate name listed in the original application and re-file online. If the rejection is contested, submit a written administrative review request to the Mercantile Section within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Registration of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público in Panama and Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a licensed Panamanian notary together with the name certificate and execute the Escritura Pública Constitutiva. The deed must state the corporate name, registered agent, shareholders, board of directors, officers, capital and by-laws. After notarization, present the deed to the Public Registry within thirty days for inscription. Once registered, request certified copies and the corporate identification card (Tarjeta de Empresa).
required_dossiers: Certificado de No Homónimo
Original incorporation deed and two clean copies
Passports or identity cards of subscribers and directors
Registered agent acceptance letter
Corporate by-laws in Spanish
Notary fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a reparo (defect notice), file a written response through a local attorney within five to ten business days, correct the deficient clause, and pay the re-valuation fee. If the deed is rejected, execute a notarial correction to the original deed and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía del Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, file the Solicitud de Aviso de Operación online or at the municipal office, designating the activity as 'electronic catalog retail of industrial MRO supplies (ISIC 4791)'. Declare estimated monthly gross sales for municipal tax purposes and pay the applicable fee. Obtain the Aviso de Operación and municipal tax certification.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered incorporation deed
Municipal application form with SIC/ISIC activity code
Lease agreement or proof of physical premises
Identification document of the legal representative
Preliminary fire inspection certificate if the premises will store goods
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality queries the activity code or premises, correct the SIC code to ISIC 4791 and submit supplementary lease or fire-safety documents. An administrative appeal may be filed before the Municipal Tax Tribunal within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Identification and Digital Signature Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the certificate of incorporation and the Aviso de Operación, pre-enroll on the DGI online portal and appoint a Panamanian Certified Public Accountant (Contador Público Autorizado). Obtain the RUC for corporate and employer purposes. Apply for the digital signature certificate (Firma Electrónica) to enable electronic filing of ITBMS and income tax returns.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered incorporation deed
Municipal Aviso de Operación
Proof of registered office address
Identity document of legal representative
CPA appointment form
Completed physical tax address form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI portal rejects the RUC application due to mismatched data, file a corrective deed before the Public Registry and resubmit the corrected documents. If the company has no payroll at formation, register as a non-employer or 'sin empleados' status to avoid interim filing obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección de Comercio Interior; no industrial manufacturing license applies to ISIC 4791 electronic catalog retail, but the municipal commercial license is compulsory.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Operation Notice) / Licencia Comercial del Municipio de Panamá

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) de la República de Panamá – Dirección de Normas y Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Actividad de Bajo Riesgo Ambiental (EIA Registration / Exempt from Full EIA Report) under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 of 2006 and Resolución AG-0325-2008. Electronic catalog MRO distribution is exempt from a full EIA unless the warehouse exceeds 1,000 square meters or stores hazardous chemical maintenance products.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary and non-hazardous wastewater must comply with MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0325-2008 discharge tables before entering municipal sewers, including pH 6-9, COD not exceeding 500 mg/L, BOD not exceeding 300 mg/L, and TSS not exceeding 300 mg/L. There are no material VOC emissions from MRO hardware storage; if lubricants or chemical maintenance products are handled, any spills must be contained and disposed of through licensed hazardous waste operators. Solid waste must be segregated and removed under municipal ordinance, with no open burning permitted.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (Certificado del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá) and structural load inspection for warehouse shelving; occupancy certificate from the Municipality; workplace health and safety review under the Dirección de Higiene y Seguridad Ocupacional of MITRADEL; and basic sanitation clearance from the Ministerio de Salud for any employee-accessible storage area or distribution center.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), consolidated within the Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos (ANIP); official portal: https://www.anip.gob.pa / https://www.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first be validly incorporated and registered in the Registro Público de Panamá, acting through a licensed Panamanian resident agent. The resident agent submits the public deed of incorporation, amended corporate articles, proof of registered agent and registered office, and identification of directors/officers to ANIP-DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). The RUC is the mandatory tax identification for all VAT/ITBMS and income tax filings. Foreign entities not yet incorporated may obtain a provisional RUC only where Panamanian-source revenue is anticipated; physically absent non-resident sellers deriving Panamanian-source e-commerce income must appoint a resident tax agent and register for ITBMS before commencing taxable sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity election exists under Panamanian law. Tax classification follows corporate law and the Código Fiscal. The Sociedad Anónima is mandatorily taxed as a corporation on Panama-source income only. Specific special-regime elections available in lieu of general territorial tax treatment include the SEM (Servicios Empresariales Multinacionales) regime for multinational headquarters and the Panama-Pacifico special economic zone regime; these elections impose alternative income tax treatment and must be registered with ANIP and SEM authorities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a las Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — a VAT-type tax on the transfer of goods and provision of services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general minimum turnover threshold; any person habitually engaged in taxable commercial, industrial or service activities in Panama must register for ITBMS before commencing activities. Small taxpayers with annual gross receipts not exceeding USD 36,000 (equivalent in PAB/ballboas) may elect the simplified small-taxpayer quota regime instead of full ITBMS compliance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing pursuant to ANIP-DGI's Sistemas de Facturación Electrónica. Taxpayers must issue invoices through the ANIP digital platform or certified private software connected by API/web services to the tax authority; each invoice receives a digital fiscal stamp and verification code (Código de Verificación) upon pre-validation. Large taxpayers are on phased mandatory e-invoicing with full national rollout targeted across all business sizes; retail and unintegrated merchants may still print authorized pre-numbered invoices or fiscal-machine receipts, but such documents must be reported to ANIP within stated deadlines. Real-time clearance is required for B2B and B2C e-commerce transactions where the supplier operates through the electronic issuance channel.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Panamanian territory are zero-rated for ITBMS provided the sale is made to a foreign purchaser and the goods leave Panama; export status is evidenced by the customs export declaration. Services consumed outside Panama, including e-commerce and MRO catalog support services rendered to non-resident B2B customers with no Panamanian use or enjoyment, qualify as territorial zero-rated (non-taxed) exports to the extent the service is not effectively connected with activities performed in Panama. The exporter must maintain proof that title and risk passed abroad and that no local consumption occurred.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ANIP-DGI may audit export transactions and, if zero-rating is assessed to be fraudulent or unsupported, will retroactively assess unpaid ITBMS at the standard rate plus daily surcharges, apply fines ranging from 100% to 200% of the omitted tax, impose business closure for repeated violations, and refer willful falsification of export declarations for criminal prosecution under the Código Fiscal and criminal law (including imprisonment). The tax statute of limitations is generally five years, extended where fraudulent or unfiled returns are found; refund claims for excess input ITBMS are subject to desk review and field audit, with denial of refund and clawback of credits previously granted if documentation is incomplete or inconsistent with customs SISCOM records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not maintain a central bank. The monetary system is fully dollarized: the United States Dollar (USD) is legal tender alongside the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) at a fixed 1:1 parity, with no fiduciary issuance of PAB paper. Banking licensing, conduct, and cross-border intermediation are supervised by the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP) pursuant to Cabinet Decree No. 328 of 1998 and SBP regulations. The Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and clearing bank for government flows. The Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) executes AML/CFT supervision under Law 23 of 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates under a fully convertible, dollarized regime with no foreign-exchange control statute. Current-account and capital-account transactions, including trade settlements, profit remittances, dividend distributions, loan servicing, and capital repatriation, require no prior authorization from any Panamanian authority; there is no BOP reporting system for individual corporate transfers. MRO e-commerce earnings are subject only to Panamanian-source income taxation on a territorial basis, and undistributed foreign or offshore-derived proceeds may be retained freely overseas. Statutory taxes on distributions such as the dividend tax are fiscal obligations, not convertibility impediments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Industrial MRO e-commerce exporters may retain 100% of export proceeds in USD or any freely convertible currency in Panama or abroad, without surrender to the Banco Nacional de Panamá. Under Law 23 of 2015, banks must retain supporting trade documentation for transactions above USD 10,000 and report anomalous accumulations of export proceeds, but no central-bank deposit or conversion requirement applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account and FX Hedging Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for disbursement-pass-through infrastructure but LOW for primary treasury settlement. Panama does not issue a standalone e-money institution (EMI) licence; fintechs such as Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, or Payoneer typically hold foreign licences and may enter Panama only as registered payment-service providers under SBP regulations or as foreign agents under Law 23 of 2015. An unlicensed offshore EMI cannot maintain a settlement account with a Panamanian clearing bank and cannot sponsor local USD ACH rails, so it should be used only to receive card-scheme settlement from the e-commerce gateway and to route supplier disbursements via SWIFT into the Panama S.A. primary account. Legal constraints include SBP licensing thresholds for digital-payment merchants, UAF suspicious-transaction reporting for stored-value floats, and contractual restrictions on card scheme fund acceptance through e-commerce stores.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: SBP due-diligence rules require the onboarding bank to identify the legal representative and all ultimate beneficial owners of the S.A. before activation. Major banks such as Banco General, Banistmo, and Global Bank generally mandate a physical appearance at the Panama City branch by at least one director or the appointed attorney-in-fact with executive authority; fully remote opening is rarely accepted for new non-resident corporate clients. Some mid-market banks such as Towerbank International and Multibank allow hybrid onboarding with notarized and apostilled corporate books, an authenticated video interview, and a Panamanian resident registered agent. Practical minimum: provide Board Resolution, Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RLB) extract, signed mandate cards, and a live validation interview for every individual holding more than 10% of capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list or negative-news hits on the S.A. shareholders, intermediate holding vehicles, or major MRO suppliers in emerging markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening report, SDN and FATF watchlist clearance, UBO register extracts showing natural persons, certified passport copies and residence proofs, shareholder declaration of source of funds and wealth, and a counterparty commercial-relationship memorandum for any supplier flagged by the bank's filtering engine.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Law 70 of 2019 economic-substance scrutiny triggered by a Panama S.A. with no local employees and cross-border digital commerce core activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Yearly economic-substance return demonstrating that order processing, payment routing, inventory coordination, and logistics control are effectively managed from Panama; registered-agent certificate of good standing; board minutes evidencing local decision-making; documented commercial rationale for MRO catalog distribution; employment or BPO agreements with third-party service providers in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High velocity of outbound B2B disbursements to multiple small suppliers, creating a fast-payment pattern inconsistent with a newly incorporated operational account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Order-to-pay transactional ledger with purchase orders, pro-forma invoices, Incoterms terms, airway bills or bill-of-lading records, and proof-of-delivery confirmations per beneficiary; written treasury disbursement policy approved by the board; quarterly AML monitoring report prepared by the registered agent or an external compliance advisor; visibility into the e-commerce platform's merchant settlement statement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections are received in USD via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers routed through the bank's New York-based correspondent network (CHIPS or Fedwire), with the transaction narrative clearly labelled as paid-in capital subscription and, where required, using purpose code GTR-7699 for commercial payments. No currency-control or central-bank filing is required. The receiving Panamanian bank will authenticate the remitting bank, verify the source of funds against the shareholder's UBO file, and post the funds to the S.A.'s capital escrow or operational account. Supporting package: certified copy of the capital-subscription resolution, the shareholders' register extract, a source-of-funds statement, and confirmation that the entity holds no bearer shares after the transitional abolition.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements employ four clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for direct USD payments to foreign suppliers or their bank accounts; (2) irrevocable documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by the Panamanian bank and advised or confirmed by a US or European correspondent for MRO purchase orders exceeding USD 50,000; (3) real-time local payment rails or virtual-account settlement in the supplier country for small-ticket disbursements below USD 5,000; and (4) card-scheme payouts through a licensed acquirer or PSP for transactions received on the electronic catalog. All rails are USD-denominated, settled via the New York correspondent, and treasury policy maintains a next-day liquidity buffer of at least 120% of the average daily disbursement ceiling.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR and USD/CNY outright deliverable forwards with SBP-licensed counterparty banks
USD/CNH cross-currency basis swaps for MRO procurement from Asian hardware suppliers
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on COP, MXN, and BRL for regional subsidiary cash-flow hedging
Vanilla FX options on USD/COP and USD/BRL purchased through authorized Panamanian dealing desks
ISDA-documented non-deliverable options (NDOs) for non-convertible Latin American currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax — Fiscal Obligation of the Corporation (Tasa Anual de Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January; no statutory grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% monthly surcharge on the unpaid amount (capped at 50%) plus legal interest. Companies with two or more consecutive unpaid years lose good standing and may be administratively dissolved or struck off by the Public Registry after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) — applicable only if Panamanian-source income is generated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year corporation, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled returns are fined at 5% of the tax due per month or fraction (maximum 50%), plus monthly late-payment interest of 1.5%. Continued delinquency freezes the tax good standing certificate ('Certificado de Cumplimiento') and blocks administrative permits and government contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (Confirmación Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) via the licensed resident agent; Panamanian Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary; within 30 days after any change in shareholding or share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain current UBO records may result in administrative fines against the corporation and/or the resident agent under Law 70 of 2017 and Executive Decree 51; the company's good standing certificate may be withheld until information is regularized.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Renewal (Renovación de Agente Residente y Oficina Registrada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed resident agent in Panama; not a government filing, but a legal maintenance requirement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the date of the annual franchise tax payment or per the registered agent's service renewal schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of the registered agent can trigger the agent's resignation, exposing the corporation to administrative strike-off by the Public Registry; reinstatement requires appointment of a new agent and payment of all outstanding fines and taxes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Panama S.A. must undergo an independent audit and file audited financial statements with the DGI when: (i) annual gross revenue exceeds US$3,000,000; or (ii) total assets exceed US$1,000,000. Additionally, entities operating under licenses, banks, insurance companies, and corporations listed on the Panama Stock Exchange are always subject to mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Panama; no separate local GAAP. Smaller entities may apply IFRS for SMEs if they satisfy the applicable exemption thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 70 of 2017, the corporation must keep a confidential UBO register with the resident agent. Upon each share transfer or change of control, the corporation must submit a sworn statement of the ultimate beneficial owner within 30 days. There is no annual statutory UBO filing in Panama; instead, the resident agent is obligated to confirm UBO information at least once each calendar year and upon any material change. Failure to maintain up-to-date information is a compliance violation subject to administrative fines.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 – US$6,000 per audit engagement, only when Panama-source income or statutory thresholds trigger an independent audit; typically not payable by a dormant offshore S.A.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on Panama-source net taxable income (territorial tax system)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-source income is outside the territorial tax base. No general tax holiday applies to an e-commerce MRO distributors' S.A.; the standard 25% rate applies. Taxpayers with gross annual revenue ≤ B/. 1,500,000 may elect the Alternative Income Tax Calculation (CAIR) regime at 4% of gross taxable revenue, which is often more favorable for low-margin trading entities. Panama Pacifico and SEM (Multinational Headquarters) incentives do not apply to ISIC 4791 e-commerce retail.
